subject: Billing math: treatment of short chats, context truncation, and pilot minimums
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@brightcart.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 4 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on billing math for short chats + pilot minimums

Hi Hannah / Ben,

We're reviewing our first month of activity and have a few billing questions before we finalize the pilot true-up. A couple of concrete items:

- Small/utility calls: we have a stream of very short assistant calls (one-line prompts, a handful of tokens). In the invoice these appear to be getting billed up to a per-call minimum which materially increases our spend versus expectations. Can you explain how short calls are rounded and whether there is any intra-day aggregation?
- Context length / truncation: some of our sessions send a 6k token context but the service responds with a short completion. How are prompt + completion tokens attributed when we change model or swap contexts mid-session?
- Pilot concessions: for evaluation we expected a smoothing or crediting policy for micro-calls. Is there standard pilot language you offer for early-stage customers?

Can you share a short worked example and, if possible, a sample invoice showing the rounding math (we can redact order IDs). I've attached a CSV export of a handful of representative calls.

Thanks — the accounting team will want an answer this week.

Elena Torres
CTO, BrightCart
elena@brightcart.com

Attachment: brightcart-microcalls-export.csv (csv)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Question on billing math for short chats + pilot minimums

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear examples, and appreciate the CSV. Quick overview and then a couple of options for the pilot smoothing we can apply.

Summary of our billing behavior (short):
- Billing quantum: charges are computed in token units but billed in a per-call quantum of 25 tokens (we round up each individual API call to the next 25-token bucket).
- Context attribution: we bill prompt + completion tokens together for that call. If you interleave model calls within the same logical session, each API request is billed independently unless you enable session bundling.
- Session bundling: for Dedicated/Private and pilot customers we can enable a daily bundling policy that aggregates micro-calls for a single origin key and bills the daily total rounded to the nearest 100 tokens.

Worked example (from your CSV):
- Call A: prompt 8 tokens, completion 6 tokens = 14 tokens -> rounded up to 25 tokens billed
- Call B: prompt 4 tokens, completion 3 tokens = 7 tokens -> rounded up to 25 tokens billed
- Without bundling these two calls = 50 tokens billed (2 x 25).
- With daily bundling (aggregate = 21 tokens): rounded to nearest 100 -> 100 tokens billed for that day (smoothing helps when you have many micro-calls but fewer than the invoice quantum).

Pilot options we can offer (choose one):
1) Micro-call smoothing (no change to list price): enable daily bundling for the pilot account; we aggregate all calls under the same API key per UTC day and round daily totals to the nearest 100 tokens.
2) Micro-call waiver (limited): waive the per-call 25-token minimum for calls < 10 tokens during the first 60 days (we'll credit back the difference on the first invoice).
3) Token credit buffer: provide a one-time 50k token credit to help offset the short-call inflation while you evaluate.

Attachments: I've attached two files with sample math and a redacted invoice: rounding-examples.xlsx and sample-invoice.pdf. Ben and Karthik are looped in if you want pricing/contract language.

If you prefer, we can combine 1 + a small token credit for the first billing period — happy to propose the exact numbers once you tell me which path you'd prefer.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt

From: Elena Torres <elena@brightcart.com>

Subject: Re: Question on billing math for short chats + pilot minimums

Thanks Hannah — this is helpful. A few follow-ups:

- Daily bundling sounds promising, but BrightCart has spikes (many microcalls some days, none other days). Can you confirm whether aggregation is per-API-key UTC day (yes) and whether we can opt into a rolling 7-day aggregation instead?
- The waiver option (calls < 10 tokens) would be ideal for the first 90 days — that would dramatically reduce noise for our QA and feature-flag tests. Would Redwood sign off on 90 days instead of 60?
- On discounts: if we move to a 12-month commit after pilot, what is the standard discount band for token rates (we're looking for something in writing to show procurement).

AP team also asked: when you apply credits/waivers, will those appear on the same invoice line as usage, or as a separate invoice credit memo? They prefer separate line items for easy reconciliation.

If you can send a short mutual action plan (M.A.P.) that lays out the concession, timing, and what we need to sign, we can move quickly.

Elena

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@brightcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, accounts-payable@brightcart.com
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 16:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on billing math for short chats + pilot minimums

Elena — appreciate the clarity. Proposed pilot concession and next steps below; I've included the MAP and DocuSign link.

Pilot concession (Redwood proposal):
- Micro-call smoothing: enable daily bundling (per-API-key, UTC day) by default. Additionally, for the pilot we will also offer an optional rolling 7-day aggregation window if you prefer smoothing across weekdays — settable in the Console and applied retroactively for pilot invoices.
- Waiver term: extendable waiver for micro-calls: calls with total prompt+completion < 10 tokens will be credited back for the first 90 days of the pilot. Credits issued as a separate invoice credit memo line for easy AP reconciliation.
- Pilot discount: 10% off per-token list price for the pilot period if BrightCart signs the 12-month commitment within 30 days of pilot end.
- Minimum: to make the concession economically viable we ask for a $10,000 monthly minimum once you convert to committed Dedicated capacity (this is negotiable; happy to model alternatives).

Example calculations (two sample days):
- Day 1 (no bundling): 4 micro-calls at 7, 9, 6, 8 tokens => all <10 tokens => all credited back under waiver (0 tokens billed)
- Day 2 (mix): 10 calls at 12 tokens each => aggregate 120 tokens; with daily bundling rounded to nearest 100 => 100 tokens billed (then pilot discount applied if signed)

AP formatting: credits will appear as separate credit-memo lines (we will provide a redacted sample on request).

Next steps:
1) I attached a short mutual_action_plan.docx laying out the timeline and sign-off items.
2) If you approve we will send a DocuSign (link below) that adds the pilot smoothing/waiver language to the evaluation agreement.
3) Ben will follow up with a formal 12-month pricing band for review.
